name: Antifa
summary: Antifa is a decentralised, militant anti-fascist current of mostly anarchist, communist and socialist activists. It treats fascism and white supremacy as threats that must be confronted directly rather than debated or left to the state, using no-platforming, direct action and collective self-defense. Its politics are anti-capitalist, anti-state and distrustful of both liberal democracy and the police, with an internationalist, anti-racist and feminist outlook.
scope: The modern autonomous antifa movement of Europe and North America, as documented by Mark Bray's handbook (2017), Rose City Antifa and scholarship on the US and German movements. It excludes the Communist-linked Antifaschistische Aktion of 1932 as a party program, the Soviet state anti-fascism, and the diverse liberal anti-fascism it rejects. Antifa has no formal doctrine, so answers reflect the anarchist or antiauthoritarian majority, with Marxist currents noted where they differ, and many economic questions are inferred.

keyFigures.name: Mark Bray
keyFigures.role: Historian and author of Antifa: The Anti-Fascist Handbook, the best-known account of the movement's ideas.

sources.title: Antifa: The Anti-Fascist Handbook
sources.author: Mark Bray
sources.usedFor: Definition of anti-fascism, self-defense, no platform, direct action, opposition to state bans, revolutionary socialism, migrant solidarity. A participant-historian's account rather than a manifesto; only parts of the text were read.

sources.title: Antifa (United States)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Composition (anarchists, communists, socialists), anti-capitalism, anti-state views, tactics, groups; first 100,000 characters read.

sources.title: Antifa (Germany)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: German factions, the split over Israel, the anarcho-communist leaning and the German authorities' view.

sources.title: About Rose City Antifa
sources.author: Rose City Antifa
sources.usedFor: Group's own statements that the state upholds white supremacy and that police work with the far right.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a focus of antifa texts; as a revolutionary socialist current its members would back guaranteed care, though many would prefer mutual aid to state provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Anti-capitalist adherents support better pay, though wage reform is reformist and rarely a stated goal; inferred from the socialist orientation.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents are anti-capitalist and aim at a revolutionary socialist alternative, so they reject the claim that markets beat collective decision-making.

public-ownership.rationale: Anarchist adherents distrust state ownership while communist ones favour it; the movement is split, so no single answer is documented.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from anti-class-rule and anti-capitalist stances; taxation by the state is not an antifa campaign issue.

unions-good.rationale: Antifa draws on labor and left traditions and anti-fascists have historically defended unions, but unions are not a stated program item.

property-fundamental.rationale: Anti-capitalist, anarchist and communist participants reject private property as a near-inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-state anarchists see regulation as futile or as state action; others welcome it. Corporate power is criticised but regulation is not a defined position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Opposes austerity and cuts, which Bray links with the crisis and poverty that feed fascist reaction.

worker-ownership.rationale: Anarchist and communist majority favour workers controlling production, though antifa itself is an anti-fascist movement and rarely spells out economic models.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Adherents distrust the state and police, wear masks to avoid state and far-right surveillance, and would reject surveillance justified by terrorism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Left-libertarian milieu commonly opposes prohibition but sources do not address drug policy.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Antifa argue hate speech is not protected and should be denied a platform, yet Bray prefers confrontation to legalistic bans and distrusts the state wielding them.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement is decentralised, anti-authoritarian and has no central leadership; strongman rule is the fascist model it opposes.

state-harmful.rationale: Most participants are anarchist or antiauthoritarian and anti-state, though communist and socialist members hold a different view of the state, so only moderate agreement.

limit-guns.rationale: Adherents stress armed self-defense and some have a tradition of armed anti-fascism; they typically oppose state disarmament of the left. Inferred from self-defense stance.

empower-police-military.rationale: Rose City Antifa says police work with the far right, and activists refuse reliance on police and the state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Left libertarian milieu typically supports decriminalisation, but the sources do not address it.

decide-locally.rationale: Decentralised autonomous groups and anti-state politics suggest local control, but nationalism-versus-localism is not discussed directly.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from left and abolitionist leanings and distrust of state policing; no stated source position.

traditional-family.rationale: Bray lists struggle against patriarchy as part of anti-fascism, and queer and feminist antifa are prominent, so adherents reject traditional family as society's foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Opposition to homophobia is central; some anarchist members dislike state marriage itself, so support is moderate rather than strong.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposing patriarchy and far-right gender politics is core to antifa; adherents back reproductive rights as a matter of bodily autonomy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Left secular milieu opposes religious right politics; adherents see religion in public life as tied to far-right and authoritarian aims.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-racism and fighting white supremacy are central; Bray ties whiteness to slavery and class rule.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Queer and feminist antifa are prominent and opposition to transphobia is stated; the constructionist claim itself is implied.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Bray identifies nationalism with the fascist pillars and antifa stresses solidarity with the disinherited of the world.

gradual-change.rationale: Bray calls anti-fascism an illiberal politics of social revolutionism and rejects reliance on electoral and legal means.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Antifa groups do migrant solidarity work and protect immigrant-rights events; anti-nativism is stated among their values.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anti-state and anti-liberal-order views suggest distrust of the UN, though internationalism is valued; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-capitalist, but free trade is not addressed; inferred from opposition to capitalist globalisation.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism is a pillar of fascism for Bray and antifa stresses international solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialist and anti-militarist leanings suggest scepticism of state military intervention, though some support armed anti-fascist struggles abroad; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Migrant solidarity and sanctuary work point to support for open borders; no source states a formal open-borders program.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmentalists participate but the movement does not take a common position on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environmentalists are among participants; climate is not a defined antifa issue.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; scepticism of techno-optimism is typical of the anarchist left but is inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Unaddressed; the anarchist and environmentalist milieu tends to oppose nuclear power, inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bray describes anti-fascism as social revolutionism and most participants describe themselves as revolutionaries.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anti-hierarchical and democratic-consensus values suggest rejecting rule by experts; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Anarchist majority rejects central planning, while some communists support it; inferred and split.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anarchists and communists differ over any market role; not addressed by sources.

land-value-tax.rationale: A tax reform of no interest to the movement; no basis for a position.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from opposition to class rule; not a stated issue.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; anti-state anarchists and some socialists disagree about state-provided income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Economic nationalism clashes with the movement's internationalism; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Anti-state majority rejects state direction, though communists would support it; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Adherents favour collective rather than small private ownership; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anarcho-communist leaning among many groups points this way, but it is not a stated demand.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not a goal of the left; anarchists dislike banks but not for market-based reasons.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class-collaborationist state bodies are a fascist form that anti-fascists oppose.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anti-authoritarian ethos, and Bray criticises Stalinism and the Comintern line.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anti-hierarchical and anti-authoritarian adherents reject hereditary rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents distrust liberal democracy and electoral politics while valuing direct, consensus democracy, so they do not endorse it as the best system as stated.

direct-votes.rationale: Consensus and direct democracy are valued in organising, but not as a claim about referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Anarcho-communist and council-communist traditions are influential in antifa; not universal.

right-to-secede.rationale: No stated position; antinationalism conflicts with some secession movements while anti-state views favour it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Antifa is anti-hierarchical and treats claims of inborn fitness to rule as part of the fascist worldview it opposes; this is inferred from that outlook rather than quoted.

political-violence-never.rationale: Bray says antifa act out of collective self-defense and by any means necessary; adherents explicitly justify force against fascists.

war-builds-character.rationale: War glorification is a fascist trait that antifa oppose.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secular left outlook and opposition to religious right politics.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Strongly opposed by an anti-authoritarian left.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Anti-capitalists oppose privatised policing and courts, although anarchists want stateless alternatives to the state.

military-superiority.rationale: Antimilitarist and internationalist, so adherents reject military primacy; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Opposition to white supremacy and ethnic nationalism is the core of the movement.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bray links fascism with class rule and the marxist and anarchist currents see class struggle as central, though anti-fascism also stresses race and gender.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Revolutionary socialist egalitarianism suggests agreement, but it is inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous rights advocates participate in the movement.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Bray cites Cesaire on Nazism as imperialism brought home; reparations specifically not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalist and civilisational unity politics are linked to far-right ideas that antifa opposes.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Solidarity and collective self-defense are central; individualistic ethics rejected.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Bray criticises fascist destruction of rights of man while valuing collective solidarity; adherents do not subordinate rights to duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmentalist participants exist; not a defined position.

limit-population.rationale: Coercive population policy is at odds with anti-authoritarianism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anarcho-primitivist strands exist but are not mainstream; split.

human-enhancement.rationale: The sources say nothing on transhumanist technology and adherents do not share a documented line, so this is a genuinely neutral placeholder.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Opposition to hierarchy and technocracy makes algorithmic rule unwelcome; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Masking, digital security and fear of state and far-right surveillance mean adherents favour strong privacy tools.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejects reactionary restoration; anti-fascism opposes far-right nostalgia.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents hold a clear revolutionary ideology; Bray urges both pragmatic organising and revolutionary aims.

direct-action.rationale: Bray contrasts legalistic strategies with direct action and activists prefer disrupting events over electoral work.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bray notes building a new world in the shell of the old and democratic consensus organising, but he defends militant means as well.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivism is a fringe strand, not typical of antifa.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marxist and anarchist traditions mention it but antifa does not emphasise it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist and anarcho-communist leanings; mutual aid is a documented practice.

production-for-use.rationale: Revolutionary socialist alternative to capitalism implies production for needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Anti-capitalist socialists hold this; antifa's core is anti-fascism so not always stressed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bray criticises Stalinism; anarchist majority rejects any dictatorship, though some communists accept it.

collective-farming.rationale: No position; anarchist and communist strands differ.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Bray ties fascism to crisis, poverty and war in a capitalist world and calls for a socialist alternative.

taxation-theft.rationale: Left-wing anti-capitalists reject the claim; anarchist anti-statism is not libertarian-propertarian.

harm-principle.rationale: Anti-authoritarian ethos matches but adherents would restrict fascists' speech by social means.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective self-defense and solidarity prominent; also protects groups against oppression.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian doctrine at odds with the movement's left collectivism.

state-as-business.rationale: Anti-capitalist adherents reject treating citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Socialist emphasis on material conditions of freedom; inferred from anti-poverty views.

media-academia-power.rationale: A right-wing claim; adherents see capital and the state as the powerful actors.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Race science is a fascist doctrine opposed by anti-racist antifa.

total-state.rationale: Totalitarian control is the opposite of the anti-authoritarian view.

national-rebirth.rationale: Palingenetic ultranationalism is the fascist idea antifa fights.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Bray treats Nazism as imperialism brought home and the movement is internationalist, so adherents reject expansionist nationalism by implication.

bound-labor.rationale: Forced labor contradicts anti-capitalist and anti-hierarchical values.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Critical theory influences on parts of the left; Bray's account of fascist-shaped discourse offers mild support.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between universalist and relativist ethics.

single-common-good.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and pluralist organising, but also class-based politics; mild disagreement inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: German antifa splits into anti-imperialists, anti-Germans and neutral groups over Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by any source; adherents are anti-nationalist but also solidary with refugees, so no clear position can be inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: No source discusses language revival; anti-nationalism and minority-language solidarity point in different directions.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' democratic control favoured by socialist and anarchist members.

school-vouchers.rationale: Left opposition to privatising education; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Bray condemns the austerity of governing parties, so adherents would not argue that deficits must be avoided; the question of stimulus itself is not discussed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Anti-capitalist, so would not hold that political freedom depends on market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Antifa is not interested in rulers' virtue; rejects rule.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-nationalist, yet many support oppressed peoples' self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Anti-militarist, but UN approval is hardly an issue for anti-state members.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Adherents are mostly secular but the sources give no view on reason as the sole guide, and anarchist and communist currents differ.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Opposes nativist welfare chauvinism and supports migrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Opposes austerity and punitive welfare conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: Revolutionary socialist, class-based politics rejects partnership with employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; Marinetti-style futurism is a fascist link.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist faction of German antifa would back it, while others would not.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Opposes patriarchy and supports feminist and queer antifa.

ban-interest.rationale: No relevant position; left favours credit reform but not religious bans.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposition to white supremacy is the movement's defining commitment, so legal race classification and segregation is rejected as a matter of course.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rose City Antifa says the state upholds white supremacy and activists see state as complicit; classic Marxist-anarchist view.

elite-replacement.rationale: Great Replacement is a far-right conspiracy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Adherents distrust elections, so no stance on the system.

national-mission.rationale: Bray ties nationalism and imperial ambition to fascism, so a national duty to export a political system is rejected by implication.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Bray names patriarchy among the systems antifa fights.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Adherents distrust elites but give a systemic rather than a moral analysis.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is a fascist practice and opposed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Rose City Antifa describes police brutality and state complicity, so accountability for abuses would be welcomed.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Antifa is anti-racist and fights white-supremacist groups, whose programs include this aim; adherents would reject it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Opposing racism, patriarchy and other oppression is stated across the sources, which implies commitment to equal worth and equal rights for all.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Internationalist but no defined position on this Marxist debate.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Indigenous rights advocates and anti-colonial views support, but not explicit.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A question from Indian politics that the sources never touch; adherents would split between universalist and minority-rights instincts.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious restrictions conflict with anti-authoritarian values.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed by any source; adherents would likely oppose religious-based state bans, but this is a weak inference from their secular, anti-authoritarian leaning.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from a secular left outlook; no source addresses school curricula.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Bray criticises the Soviet Popular Front and Stalin's priorities; anarchist majority rejects state strengthening.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democratic consensus values; adherents reject state authority anyway.

population-transfer.rationale: Antifa defends migrants and opposes ethnic nationalism, so forced removal of minorities is rejected by implication.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Bray describes antifa as willing to use force by any means necessary against organised fascists, which many see as pre-emptive, so adherents reject an absolute rule against initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social-Darwinist struggle is a fascist theme; solidarity is valued.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Bray says militant antifa oppose state bans partly because they hit the left more than the right.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-hierarchy and anti-domination ethos; republican term not used.

separated-powers.rationale: Anti-state adherents see checks as irrelevant.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anarchist majority and Bray's criticism of Stalinism; Marxist-Leninist strands differ.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Solidarity with the disinherited of the world.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing-policy question with no antifa position; socialists and anarchists would split on selling public housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Antifa sits in the radical labor-friendly left, so restricting strikes would be opposed; labor law itself is not a documented focus.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Bray attributes poverty and crisis to the social and economic order, not population; inferred as the sources do not address Malthusianism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: This is a far-right claim; migrant solidarity and anti-nativism in antifa groups imply rejection.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not mentioned in the sources; anarchist sympathy for non-electoral selection is offset by communists who do not share it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Anti-state, and fearful of state repression.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and anti-poverty concern; no source discusses price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Antifa is anti-authoritarian and suspicious of state control of information, though it also seeks to deny platforms to fascists; only a weak inference.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rejects party-state militarism as part of its anti-authoritarian and anti-Stalinist stance, per Bray's criticism of Soviet-aligned communism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Given migrant solidarity and sanctuary work, adherents would oppose obstacles to citizenship; the question itself is not covered.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Fits the egalitarian, anti-hierarchy tradition of anarchism and the Paris Commune, but no source states it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Decentralised and non-partisan movement; anarchist influence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: No position; EU is a liberal institution disliked by many.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrated executive power over the military runs against anti-authoritarian politics; this is inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not discussed; anti-hierarchical views suggest mild disagreement with episcopal governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Antifa opposes authoritarian religious-right politics and theocratic rule follows from the anti-authoritarian and secular position.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A revolutionary-left principle held in the Marxist tradition; antifa as a movement does not state it, so this is inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and culturally progressive, so state moral censorship is opposed; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Antifa regards personal rule as a fascist route, so removing term limits is disliked; the issue is not discussed directly.

recall-officials.rationale: Direct-democratic and consensus organising supports recall, though adherents distrust electoral politics and give it little attention.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anti-militarist and anti-imperialist leaning implies support, but no source addresses alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists favour tenants' organising rather than a ban on renting, so adherents would disagree mildly.

people-in-arms.rationale: Bray notes militia traditions such as the Arditi del Popolo and collective self-defense, though replacing the army is not stated.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: A romantic-agrarian claim that is not part of antifa thought; inferred disagreement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: No source addresses national reunification; anti-nationalism and anti-imperialism pull in opposite directions.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: An anti-intellectual populist trope; activist culture is heavily university-linked, but this is inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anti-racism implies rejecting hierarchies of cultures, though sources do not use this wording.

death-penalty.rationale: The state executing people runs against adherents' anti-state and anti-police stance, but no source addresses capital punishment.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is a stated aim, so adherents would back it, though no source speaks to school curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular left outlook implies rejection; unaddressed in the sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Adherents split between anti-censorship libertarian and anti-patriarchy feminist views; no source speaks to it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship is a nativist ethnic principle that antifa fights; inferred from anti-nativism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Likely supported given anti-racism and minority solidarity, but not documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between protecting minorities and secular equal law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Countercultural and queer-friendly milieu and anti-authoritarian values suggest agreement; not stated.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Solidarity with the world's disinherited; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-capitalist and anti-imperialist views imply that formal independence without economic transformation is hollow; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Adherents distrust parliamentary politics yet value democratic assemblies; no stated position.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Anti-authoritarian ethos rejects authoritarian modernisation, though not specifically discussed.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Bray calls for solidarity with the disinherited of the world, though anarchist members would prefer mutual aid to state aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anti-militarist; no source discusses nuclear weapons, so this is inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A constitutional-design question the movement has no position on.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; left and anti-austerity leaning suggests mild opposition to insulating monetary policy from democratic control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalist insistence on historic land runs against antifa's anti-nationalism, but the issue divides German antifa over Israel.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Bray criticises Stalinist USSR; anarchist majority holds this.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmentalists take part in the movement, but no source states a position on risk regulation.

collective-defense.rationale: Antimilitarist and anti-NATO instincts suggest disagreement, but this is not addressed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The anti-imperialist faction of German antifa, the largest, would accept this; inferred, and the Israel question splits groups.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: As an anti-state current, antifa would not want the state to control churches, though it opposes religious hierarchy; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Anti-state and anti-hierarchical, antifa rejects the office of head of state, so a unifying figurehead is not endorsed; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: An anti-state, internationalist current opposes states using the military to hold regions; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The anarchist majority favours decentralised, self-governing communities; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Antifa is anti-authoritarian and anti-hierarchical, so a sacred ruler is the opposite of its outlook.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Anti-capitalist adherents favour redistribution over a flat rate, but taxation is rarely discussed; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Anti-racism and social change rest on circumstances shaping people; not an explicit doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Antifa distrusts state power and holds that authorities must be accountable; a ruler above the law runs against its anti-authoritarian principles.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a stated concern; anti-capitalist adherents would likely prioritise problems on Earth; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Anarchist and communist majorities reject blending in elite rule; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Antifa opposes hierarchy and fascist leader worship, so a leader cult is rejected.

equal-parenting.rationale: A feminist, egalitarian outlook suggests support for shared parenting; custody law is not addressed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Inferred from anarchist and communist distrust of party hierarchies, which the movement holds could reinstate domination.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist, egalitarian outlook; land reform is not a specific demand.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from its pro-migrant, anti-border internationalism; right of return is not specifically documented.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: It is internationalist and anti-nationalist, and rejects ethnic claims to territory as fascist.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: It is secular and anti-authoritarian, and opposes state coercion over belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: Its feminist outlook opposes legal control of women's dress.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between anti-EU and anti-nationalist views.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from its anti-racist rejection of ethnic nationalism and pan-nationalist projects.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Anti-statist adherents favor self-determination, but this specific model is not addressed, so inferred as split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from its internationalist, anti-racist call to fight racism where it occurs.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist currents in it hold this view, while anarchists stress hierarchy and ideas, so the answer is inferred and contested.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anti-capitalist adherents oppose concentrated power but distrust the state as enforcer, so inferred as split.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalist and anti-state stance; public rescue of banks is hostile to its principles.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of liberal democracy and defense of minorities against majorities, not majority supremacy.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from its feminist and egalitarian outlook.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism; autarkic blocs conflict with it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anti-capitalist adherents distrust trade deals but welcome labor standards, so inferred as split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from anarchist and communist ideals of solidarity over wage incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Its stress is on collective self-defense and mass action against fascists, not on a vanguard starting revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Its anarchist and communist majority opposes hierarchy and inherited privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Internationalist and anti-nationalist, antifa would oppose nation-centred history teaching; inferred from its rejection of nationalism, not stated on curricula.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Antifa is anti-racist and anti-imperialist, so rule over other peoples for their supposed improvement is rejected as a colonial justification.

patriotic-education.rationale: Antifa rejects nationalism and treats flag-and-anthem patriotism as a vehicle for the far right, so it opposes schooling in national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Adherents are anti-racist and see racial preferences as redress for systemic white supremacy, so abolishing them is opposed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Anarchist adherents distrust state money while Marxist ones back public banking; antifa texts say nothing, so the current is split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: As an anti-capitalist current it holds that capitalism is crisis-prone and ultimately unsustainable; inferred, since adaptability is not discussed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: An anti-imperialist, anti-state current rejects a state projecting influence over its predecessor empire's lands; inferred from those principles.

delink-world-market.rationale: Antifa is internationalist and anti-capitalist, but delinking is a development-theory question it does not address, and adherents would differ.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Most adherents stress shared working-class interests and solidarity, so the labor-aristocracy thesis is rejected, though some Marxist currents accept it; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Antifa treats discrimination as part of white supremacy and rejects any freedom to refuse service on racial grounds.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Anarchist and anti-state adherents distrust constitutional limits enforced by state courts and the state itself, though many defend civil rights; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: As internationalists hostile to the state and colonialism, antifa would deny binding force to imposed borders; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Anarchist antifa reject rulers altogether and so neither elect nor inherit them; the question is not addressed.

minority-veto.rationale: Anarchist consensus practice leans towards the veto, while Marxist currents prefer majority discipline; adherents are split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Antifa hold direct resistance to oppressive authority as legitimate and distrust the state, though the framing around constitutional law is not theirs.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Antifa are anti-state and prefer direct action and self-organisation to parliaments, so supremacy of any legislature is not their position.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal liberation is common in the anarchist and vegan milieu around antifa, though it is not a stated antifa principle.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Many in the anarchist and vegan scene reject animal exploitation, but this is not antifa doctrine; inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Antifa favour mutual aid and solidarity from below, and reject paternalist duty of the privileged; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Antifa stress active direct action and confrontation of fascists, so withdrawal from politics is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Antifa draw on anarchist and Marxist critique, which holds that media and consumer culture reproduce the existing order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian ideas of hegemony are part of the Marxist currents, though anarchists stress force and the state too; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Antifa are anti-capitalist and internationalist, and the Marxist and anarchist traditions they come from hold that imperialism extracts value from the poor.

native-born-offices.rationale: Antifa are internationalist and anti-racist and stand with migrants against nativist politics.

party-own-road.rationale: Antifa are internationalists who stress autonomy from party centres; inferred, as it concerns party relations the movement does not run.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Antifa do not address development strategy; anti-imperialist adherents distrust loans and investment but favour solidarity.

return-lost-territory.rationale: As internationalists hostile to nationalism, antifa oppose revanchist territorial claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Antifa support decolonisation and indigenous solidarity, but as anti-hierarchical anarchists they reject political rule by any group; adherents split.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism is antifa's defining value, though anarchist adherents distrust constitutions and the state; the idea is inferred as supportive with reservations.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Antifa reject the equation of fascism with communism, and Bray argues against equating anti-fascism with totalitarian theory.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Antifa hold that slavery and white supremacy were the cause, in line with the mainstream scholarship they cite.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Antifa take part in campaigns to remove Confederate and colonial monuments; the movement treats them as honouring white supremacy.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Antifa are feminist and see gender inequality as running against women; the men's-issues framing is inferred to be rejected.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Antifa are feminist and take the standard gendered analysis of domestic violence; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Antifa are internationalists who reject civilizational hierarchies, though they stress that other peoples decide for themselves; mixed, inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Antifa are anti-state and anarchist or communist, and reject any political role for the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: The socialist and feminist traditions antifa draw on call for valuing unpaid reproductive work.

filial-duty.rationale: Antifa texts do not address filial obligation; anarchist and communist members split between traditional family duty and rejecting family hierarchy.

office-by-exam.rationale: Anti-state and anti-hierarchical, antifa would reject a bureaucratic examination elite, preferring popular or collective selection; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Anti-capitalists would dislike both corporate takeovers and state-protected national capital; nationalist protectionism is not an antifa position.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: As a feminist, libertarian-left current, it favours personal freedom and rejects state moralism on marriage; stated feminism makes this a settled view among adherents.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Anarchist and council-democratic currents favour mandated, instantly recallable delegates in place of representative autonomy.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Anti-capitalist and socialist members would oppose privatised individual pension accounts in favour of collective provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Anti-capitalist and anarchist members favour common ownership of land with use-based possession; inferred from the anti-property orientation.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Anti-state anarchist members reject representative institutions as such, though some socialists would accept parliamentary control; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Internationalist, pro-migrant and anti-nationalist, antifa would oppose forced single-language policy that restricts minorities.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Internationalist and anti-nationalist; bans on foreign land ownership are nationalist, though anti-landlord views complicate this (inferred).

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-racist antifa holds that the state and institutions uphold white supremacy structurally, which fits judging policies by outcomes.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Anti-capitalist critique of commodity culture is common, but consumerism is not a central antifa topic; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anti-imperialist and anti-state, antifa opposes state covert wars; some members back foreign revolutionary groups such as Rojava, so this is inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Internationalist and anti-imperialist adherents oppose great-power invasion of allies to enforce loyalty.

corporate-influence.rationale: Antifa are anti-capitalist and see the state as serving capital and the powerful, so they would agree that business money captures government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: antifa distrust state control of civil society, though the issue is not addressed; many would also oppose it as a tool against activist groups.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist, migrant-solidarity outlook, which rejects nationalist population policy as a substitute for immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: anti-gentrification housing activism pulls toward agreeing, while migrant solidarity and opposition to exclusion pull against it.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the socialist orientation; some anarchist adherents would prefer mutual aid to any state employer.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred: antifa are suspicious of liberal democracy and Western state power, and do not rest hopes for peace on democracy promotion.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The anarchist and anti-state majority holds that law has no claim of its own and openly defends direct action and illegal tactics against fascists.

non-intervention.rationale: Adherents are split: anti-imperialism opposes foreign interference, but internationalist solidarity backs groups such as those in Rojava.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from the anarcho-syndicalist and communist currents in the movement, which favour industry-wide worker organisation; not a stated antifa position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Antifa treat fascist and far-right conspiracy claims about minorities as core propaganda to be fought, and defend minorities against them.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Anarchist and feminist currents criticise state marriage, but many adherents back marriage equality and the issue is not central.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-state, anti-secrecy outlook and its use of public research into far-right groups; not directly stated.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from anarchist and anti-capitalist localism; the movement has no stated position on supply chains.

informal-organisation.rationale: Antifa is described as decentralised, built on small autonomous groups and networks rather than parties or federations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Antifa are internationalist and anti-state, and reject nationalist claims that the national state has the last word.

religious-nation.rationale: Antifa are anti-racist and oppose religious and ethnic nationalism as a form of the far right they confront.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: As an anti-hierarchical, anti-state current, adherents reject ritual submission of weaker states to a power; inferred from anarchist and internationalist principles.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Internationalist, solidarity-minded activists favour sharing resources rather than regions hoarding revenue; inferred, as antifa texts do not address fiscal federalism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Anarchist-communist and Marxist currents distinguish personal belongings from commonly held means of production; inferred from the movement's anti-capitalist orientation.

defeat-communism.rationale: Antifa is largely made up of anarchists, communists and socialists, so a campaign to defeat communism runs against its own composition and politics.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Anti-capitalist adherents would resist private providers profiting from public services, though many prefer mutual aid to state provision; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marxist and anarchist traditions in the movement treat religion as a product of social conditions, but antifa has no doctrine on it and many members work with religious allies; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The anarchist majority regards capitalism as harmful rather than a necessary stage, while Marxist currents would partly agree; inferred from the anti-capitalist consensus.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Antifa is described as feminist and anti-capitalist, and its socialist and anarchist wings tie gender oppression to capitalism and the state.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialist and feminist strands favour collective provision of care work; antifa texts do not address it, so this is inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Antifa is internationalist and anti-nationalist, with migrant solidarity central to its politics, so enforced linguistic purity of a national language is rejected.

treaties-binding.rationale: Antifa backs indigenous and anti-colonial struggles, but its anti-state anarchist majority does not treat state treaties as authoritative; inferred, mild agreement.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The anarchist and antiauthoritarian majority favours self-governing, commonly owning communities and federations; antifa texts do not set this out as a programme.

majority-settlement.rationale: Antifa is anti-racist, anti-colonial and committed to migrant and minority solidarity, so state-steered settlement to dilute minority regions is opposed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anarchist and antiauthoritarian activists reject both capitalism and state communism, but antifa has no formal doctrine on a third way; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Antifa opposes blood-and-soil nationalism and fascist myths of ancestral entitlement.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Opposing fascism and its antisemitism is antifa's reason to exist, so denying the Holocaust is rejected.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Defending LGBT people against the far right is a standard antifa cause.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Anarchist adherents oppose state repression, though they would deny fascists the ability to organise; read literally this is mostly rejected.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Anarchist and secular adherents reject state enforcement of religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Antifa is anti-imperialist and anti-colonial, rejecting exploitation of subject territories.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Antifa is secular and does not take a religious-duty frame, but opposes foreign invasion; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: a secular, anti-authoritarian movement would not endorse theocratic uprising, though it opposes the rulers' repression.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Anarchist and anti-authoritarian majority favours direct, horizontal decision-making and autonomous organising.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Bray's handbook and Rose City Antifa treat racism, sexism, homophobia and capitalism as intertwined struggles.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Defending transgender people is part of the movement's anti-fascist platform.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not a stated theme; inferred from bodily-autonomy leanings of the movement.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Antifa places itself on the revolutionary left and rejects the 'third position' that blends left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist anarchist and Marxist outlook; not discussed in the sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Antifa opposes anti-Muslim racism and the far-right claim of civilisational incompatibility.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Anarchist and secular adherents reject divine authority as well as state authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: adherents are secular but oppose bans that single out Muslims, so on balance would reject the ban.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with survivors of harassment; not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Reformist capitalism is rejected by an anti-capitalist movement, though adherents would back some protections; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anarchist anti-militarism, though armed self-defence is accepted; inferred, and Marxist currents differ.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian anti-capitalism: unequal wealth first is rejected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and opposition to NATO-style blocs; not stated in the sources.

missingStatements.text: Fascists should be denied a platform to speak and organise rather than debated.
missingStatements.rationale: No platforming organised fascists, rather than answering them in debate, is Bray's central strategic claim and antifa's defining tactic.
missingStatements.declined: Tactic specific to antifa (no-platforming); few other ideologies would take a side beyond the hate-speech item, and the bank is kept lean.

missingStatements.text: People are justified in using physical force to stop fascist groups from organising.
missingStatements.rationale: Antifa describe their use of force as collective self-defense against fascist violence and organising.

missingStatements.text: The police and courts cannot be relied on to protect people from the far right.
missingStatements.rationale: Rose City Antifa says police work with far-right aggressors and the state upholds white supremacy; the Torch network principle is not to rely on police.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow claim about police reliability; covered in spirit by empower-police-military and security-forces-accountable.

notes: Antifa is a tactic-defined, non-hierarchical movement, so economic and institutional answers are mostly inferred from its anarchist and communist majority; low-confidence answers are numerous. German antifa splits into anti-imperialist, anti-German and Israel-neutral factions (s3), so Israel-related answers are neutral.
